evidence_type: Meta-analysis 17 prospective studies n=1.98M (Yao & Tian 2014); high HDL-C inversely associated with CRC risk (pooled RR 0.84 95%CI 0.69-1.02)
clinical_implication: Low HDL is a candidate CRC risk marker; assay already in routine clinical chemistry panels

evidence_type: Retrospective cohort n=1270 CRC patients (Xie 2024); low ApoA-I (<0.9 g/L) predicts shorter PFS/OS
clinical_implication: Adds prognostic information beyond stage; could refine post-resection surveillance

known_pathway: Plasma proteomic biomarker for CRC detection
evidence_type: Quantitative MS + microarray validation (Murakoshi 2011); ApoA-I differentiates CRC from healthy plasma (p<1e-3)
clinical_implication: Supports ApoA-I as discovery-grade circulating biomarker

evidence_type: Narrative review (Gupta 2021); pre-operative serum albumin predicts CRC surgical outcomes and prognosis
clinical_implication: Cheap routine marker of nutrition/cachexia; integrated into pre-op risk scores

evidence_type: Same review (Gupta 2021); total protein and prealbumin track nutritional status in CRC
clinical_implication: Co-traveler with albumin; reflects hepatic synthetic function

evidence_type: AMORIS cohort + meta-analysis (Monroy-Iglesias 2021); STB NOT associated with CRC risk despite antioxidant rationale
clinical_implication: Honest null finding; supports cautious interpretation of bilirubin as a CRC biomarker

evidence_type: Mendelian randomisation (Burgess 2018) established Lp(a) causal in CHD; CRC-specific evidence limited
clinical_implication: Cardiovascular comorbidity context; should not be claimed as a primary CRC marker on this evidence base

evidence_type: UK Biobank NMR multidisease model (Buergel 2022 Nat Med) trained on 168 NMR markers across 24 conditions including cancers
clinical_implication: Subfraction-level resolution refines crude HDL-C; promising integrated NMR risk panel

known_pathway: NMR lipoprotein subfraction (LDL particle TG content)
evidence_type: Meta-analysis (Yao & Tian 2014) shows high serum TG associated with CRC risk (RR 1.18 95%CI 1.04-1.34)
clinical_implication: Triglyceride-rich LDL is a candidate dyslipidaemia axis in CRC etiology

evidence_type: NutriNet-Sante prospective cohort (Diallo 2017) and IARC Group 1 designation specifically for colorectal cancer
clinical_implication: Diet modifiable; processed meat reduction is established public-health recommendation for CRC prevention
